title: Lathe geometry with creases, caps and exact volume
purpose: Revolve a 2D profile around Y into a three.js mesh with smooth normals that split where the profile turns sharply, flat caps on open ends, closed-loop profiles for rings and arc-length UVs, plus the exact volume and area of the revolved shape. Use it for vases, bottles, chess pieces, lamps and turned props.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: latheProfileData, latheProfileVolume and latheProfileArea need no three.js; createLatheProfileGeometry takes three.js as THREE; only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: latheProfileData
exports.summary: The revolved profile as typed arrays; the outside is to the right of the profile direction.

exports.name: createLatheProfileGeometry
exports.summary: The same data in a BufferGeometry with an index and computed bounds.

exports.name: latheProfileVolume
exports.summary: Signed volume of the full-turn solid: sum of pi / 3 (r0^2 + r0 r1 + r1^2) (y1 - y0).

exports.name: latheProfileArea
exports.summary: Area of the full-turn surface without caps: sum of pi (r0 + r1) times segment length.

inputs.profile: array of [r, y] points with r >= 0, consecutive points distinct; drawn bottom to top on the outside

options.name: phiStart
options.meaning: Angle of the first column (x = r sin phi, z = r cos phi).

options.name: phiLength
options.meaning: Swept angle; less than a full turn leaves the sides open.

options.name: creaseAngle
options.meaning: A profile vertex turning by more than this gets two rings with their own normals.

options.name: caps
options.meaning: Close open profile ends that are off the axis with flat caps.

options.name: closed
options.meaning: The profile is a loop (last point joins the first), for rings and tori.

limits: The profile is a polyline: smooth curves need enough points (sample your spline first). The outside is the right-hand side of the profile direction, so a profile drawn top to bottom comes out inside out. Caps are flat discs at the end heights and assume the profile ends off the axis; a partial sweep (phiLength under a full turn) leaves its two cut faces open. Vertices on the axis repeat once per column, as in LatheGeometry. latheProfileVolume and latheProfileArea describe the smooth surface of revolution; the mesh with N segments has the volume times (N / 2 pi) sin(2 pi / N). Self-intersecting profiles are not detected. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Surface of revolution with per-vertex profile normals
Crease splitting by the turning angle between profile segments
Frustum volume pi h / 3 (r0^2 + r0 r1 + r1^2) and Pappus's theorems
